question.text: Half of the space between the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $K$. The remaining half contains air as shown in the figure. The capacitor is now given a charge $Q$. Then

options.text: electric field in the dielectric-filled region is higher than that in the air-filled region
on the two halves of the bottom plate the charge densities are unequal
charge on the half of the top plate above the air-filled part is $\frac{Q}{K+1}$
capacitance of the capacitor shown above is $(1+K) \frac{C_{0}}{2},$ where $C_{0}$ is the capacitance of the same capacitor with the dielectric removed.
